document.body:
Integration review, first 100 days of the overseas unit
Review by the project management office of KEC International, July 2026.
The purchase and invoice systems of the acquired unit were cut over on day 21, before the
process owners were agreed. Site teams rebuilt their old steps as 14 workarounds outside the new
system. Local labour, contract and payment terms were first reviewed on day 63. That review took
more time than was planned at close.
What happened in the first 100 days
Day Event
Day 0 Close of the acquisition. One integration lead was named. No process owner was
named.
Day 21 System cut-over for purchase orders and supplier invoices.
Day 21 to day 45 Site teams kept spreadsheets beside the new system for purchase requests, goods
receipts and subcontractor bills. The count on day 45 was 14 workarounds.
Day 63 First review of local labour rules, contract terms and payment cycles. Subcontractors on
site were paid every two weeks, and the group system paid once a month.
Day 80 Process owners were named for purchase to payment, site payroll and subcontractor
billing.
Day 100 9 of the 14 workarounds were closed. The other 5 each have an owner and a closing
date.
Why it went this way
The cut-over date was fixed in the plan at close and was not tied to a sign-off.
Process ownership was treated as a task for the weeks after the cut-over.
The review of local labour, contract and payment terms had no date in the plan.
What the next integration should do
1. Name the owner of each core process before day 0.
2. Start a system cut-over only after the process owner signs off the target process.
3. Review local labour, contract and payment terms by day 30.
4. Keep one list of workarounds, each with an owner and a closing date, and read it every week.
Numbers of this review
What was counted Count
Workarounds counted on day 45 14
Workarounds closed by day 100 9
Workarounds open on day 100, each with an owner 5

Days from the system cut-over to the naming of the process owners 59
Synthetic sample written for the RPG NeuralMesh demonstration. It is not a record of KEC International.
